reading.body:
Steven Horsford's AI record is mostly money and bills, not votes: nine PAC contributions from five companies and four AI-related bills in eighteen months.

The pattern is a legislator who takes AI money and writes AI law at the same time. Meta, Google, Amazon, Oracle, and Microsoft PACs gave between $1,000 and $5,000 across 2025 and 2026. In the same window he sponsored the AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act, cosponsored the AI Tax Integrity Act of 2026 and the AI Impersonation Prevention Act of 2025, and voted yes on four bills that passed under suspension of the rules. The contributions and the bills are listed in date order, and the data does not claim one caused the other.

For AI specifically, this is the legislative layer of the buildout. Compute is constrained by power and buildings, and those constraints get shaped by tax treatment, job-impact disclosure, and impersonation liability, which is exactly the ground these four bills cover. The companies funding data center construction are the same companies writing checks here.

What the data does not show is what any of these bills would do, whether the votes were close, or whether the money changed anything. It also does not cover committee work, private meetings, or positions taken outside recorded votes. One contribution appears twice on the same date from the same PAC, and the record does not explain whether that is two filings or a duplicate.
